title: GitHub - maxtechstack/ai-support-checker: Count what your AI support agent closed on its own and what it handed back, from a Gorgias ticket export. Runs in your browser; your file never leaves your computer.
excerpt: Count what your AI support agent closed on its own and what it handed back, from a Gorgias ticket export. Runs in your browser; your file never leaves your computer. - maxtechstack/ai-support-checker
content_html:
Drop in a Gorgias ticket export and see how many tickets your AI agent closed on its own, how many it handed back to your team, and how many of its closes were post-purchase exceptions (damaged, missing or wrong items, order changes, return exceptions) that need an action outside the helpdesk.

The screenshot uses a synthetic file from samples/. No real tickets are in this repo.

Nothing leaves your browser

The file is read and counted in your browser, in a Web Worker. There is no upload, no account, no API call, and no analytics on the file. Only counts are ever shown: no ticket text, names, emails or order numbers.

How to check this yourself:

  • DevTools: open the page, open DevTools → Network, then drop your file. No request appears while it's processed.
  • Offline: load the page, turn off Wi-Fi, then drop your file. It works the same.
  • The code: the page's Content-Security-Policy sets connect-src 'none', so the browser itself blocks any request from page code. test/privacy.test.js checks the code for network calls, and the Playwright test asserts zero requests while a file is processed.

Run it

In the browser: closewellhq.com/check/, or locally:

npm run build && npm run serve      # http://127.0.0.1:8788/check/

From the command line (Node 20+, no install needed):

node cli/check.js export.csv          # the same summary the page shows
node cli/check.js export.csv --json   # the counts as JSON

The page and the CLI share core/, so they give the same numbers for the same file.

How to get the export: docs/how-to-export-from-gorgias.md.

How it counts

  • AI-handled: the ticket has a Gorgias AI Agent tag (ai_close, ai_handover, ai_snooze, ai_processing, ai_answered, ai_executed_action, ai_failed_action) or a value in the "AI Agent Outcome" ticket field (Close::, Handover:: or Snooze::, used only when there is no AI tag). ai_ignore alone doesn't count.
  • Closed by AI: ai_close and the ticket is closed. Handed back: ai_handover (it wins over ai_close). ai_answered sits next to every outcome and is never an outcome by itself. Snoozed (ai_snooze) counts as still open, even though Gorgias exports snoozed tickets with a Closed date.
  • Action recorded: on tickets the AI closed alone, ai_executed_action means it completed an action in Shopify or another connected app, and ai_failed_action means an action couldn't complete. The "Resolution" ticket field, when filled, is shown as context only. Neither shows whether a refund, reship or 3PL change actually happened.
  • Customers who came back after an AI close aren't counted: Gorgias removes ai_close when a ticket reopens, so the export shows only the last state.
  • Categories: the "AI Intent" ticket field when its first two levels are in the rules (e.g. order::damaged); otherwise keyword and tag rules on the subject, tags and contact reason, with English plus basic German, French, Spanish and Dutch lists. A ticket gets the first match in priority order. It's an estimate.

The AI Agent tags, the "AI Agent Outcome" values and the tag separator were checked on Nov 22, 2026 with 5 tickets on a Gorgias trial connected to a Shopify development store (samples/edge/gorgias-ai-real-tags.csv, anonymized).

Change the rules

All rules live in two files:

  • rules/gorgias.json: header names, AI Agent tags (outcome and action tags), the "AI Agent Outcome" prefixes and the "Resolution" values.
  • rules/categories.json: AI Intent values, keywords per category and language, and tags that map to a category.

After editing, run npm run rules (writes core/rules-data.js, which the page loads), then npm test. If the results change on purpose, npm run golden updates the expected outputs; review the diff.

Develop

npm test            # unit tests, golden outputs, privacy checks (Node's built-in runner)
npm run samples     # regenerate the synthetic CSVs in samples/
npm run e2e         # build + Playwright in Google Chrome: zero requests, no ticket text, page = CLI, 50,000 rows < 10 s
npm run copy-check  # words-to-avoid check on user-facing copy

Plain JavaScript (ES2020) with JSDoc types, no framework, no build step for the page. PapaParse is vendored in web/vendor/ (MIT).
